newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-British HTV concedes it's a bid target.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-British HTV concedes it's a bid target.

text.p: Britain's regional television broadcaster HTV Group reported a 10 percent rise in half-year pretax profits at the top end of expectations on Wednesday and conceded that it was a takeover target.
But chairman Louis Sherwood insisted that the group still saw an independent future, sending HTV shares slipping on a market hoping for news of a takeover bid.

Sherwood said: "We recognise that HTV, as one of the few remaining independent Channel 3 licensees, is of real strategic value to the major ITV (independent television) companies, especially in relation to the airtime sales (advertising) house structure."
"However we continue to see a strong independent future for HTV," he said in the results statement.

HTV, whose area straddles Wales and the west of England, raised half-year pretax profits to 6.7 million pounds ($10.5 million) from 6.1 million a year ago and lifted half year dividend 12 percent to 1.4 pence.
Traders said the figures looked healthy but said they were looking for bid news. HTV shares, which have surged to a 12-month high of 404 pence on bid hopes, slipped 1.5 pence to 352p.
"Investors had hoped for some news of takeover bids in today's statement but it was pretty vague stuff," one marketmaker said.
As big television players race for supremacy in Britain's terrestrial television network, speculation of a bid has focused on ITV broadcasting giants Carlton Communications or United News & Media.
HTV's chief executive Chris Rowlands told Reuters in an interview that he met with groups that had been tipped as bidders two or three times a week to discuss "industry issues".
But he declined to comment on whether these talks had included a bid for the company. "Within our industry we are in talks with everybody all the time," Rowlands said.
HTV core broadcasting business saw operating profits before licence payments rise four percent to 16.4 million pounds. Total net advertising revenue rose 2.5 percent to 48.9 million pounds.
Its growing rights division, Harvest Entertainment, which it has called the "engine" for growth prospects, lifted operating profits by a sturdy 19 percent to 2.5 million pounds.
HTV, whose productions include a version of Enid Blyton's childrens book "The Famous Five", is investing 10 million pounds in the next nine months in new digital technology.
The investment should boost efficiency and reduce franchise costs by over 2.5 million pounds per year. The group said it would levy an exceptional item to cover costs in the full year.

Last month, media and leisure company Granada Group confirmed it had raised its shareholding in Yorkshire-Tyne Tees Television to an effective 27 percent by exercising warrants. Some analysts still expect a full takeover. ($1=.6387 Pound)
